title: VASIO local control API v1 messages

supervisionMidiObservations.description: MIDI traffic the engine observed. Every application port goes through an engine-owned loopback, so its traffic is observable; counters cover MIDI 1.0 messages since engine start and survive configuration changes.

activity.description: Every MIDI 1.0 message from the port except timing clock (F8) and active sensing (FE).

clock.description: Timing clock (F8) arriving from the port. running: a tick arrived less than 1 s ago. bpm: smoothed tempo at 24 ticks per quarter note, null until 2 ticks or when stopped. echoSuspected: the engine also sends clock to this port, so these ticks may be its own clock coming back (MIDI thru) rather than a real source. transport: last start (FA), continue (FB) or stop (FC).

clockSources.description: Ports where timing clock is currently arriving. Each application sends through its own In loopback, so the port identifies the emitting application or device. Entries with echoSuspected are likely the engine's own clock coming back.

midiTimebase.description: Time reference for MIDI timing. soundCard: the physical ASIO driver's frame count, fitted against the Windows clock over about 30 s; MIDI clock tempo and scheduling follow the card's real frequency. windows: no card is running.

measuredSampleRate.description: Card frames per second of Windows time; null until measured (about 2 s).

midiEngineClock.description: Clock generated by the engine by counting sound card frames: it never drifts from the audio.

midiVirtualPort.description: Application port: a dedicated MIDI 1.0 "<name> In" port (the application sends to the patchbay) and "<name> Out" port (the patchbay sends to the application). Each direction is its own Windows MIDI Services Basic MIDI 1.0 Loopback and can be turned on or off without touching the other; at least one is required. No MIDI 2.0 port is created. API port id: midi:virtual:<id>.

name.description: Base name; applications see "<name> In" and "<name> Out".

input.description: Create "<name> In"; the port can then be a route source.

output.description: Create "<name> Out"; the port can then be a route destination.

midiRoute.description: Directed link between two MIDI 1.0 ports. Port ids are midi:virtual:<id> or midi:port:<group 1-16>:<Windows MIDI Services endpoint device id of a native MIDI 1.0 device>; each group of an endpoint is one MIDI 1.0 port, as MIDI 1.0 applications see it. Channels are 1-based. Only MIDI 1.0 devices are offered and only MIDI 1.0 messages are routed; MIDI 2.0 endpoints and messages are ignored. midi:clock:engine is the engine-generated clock and can only be a source.

channels.description: Accepted source channels for channel voice messages; default all.

transpose.description: Semitones applied to note numbers; notes moved out of 0..127 are dropped.

reclock.description: Re-emit the source's timing clock (F8) on a regular grid timed by the sound card instead of forwarding each tick as it arrives. One tick out per tick in: the source tempo and beat position are kept, arrival jitter is removed. Ignored when the source is midi:clock:engine.

engineClock.description: Saved tempo of the engine clock. Transport is not saved: the clock starts stopped.

name.description: MIDI 1.0 port name as Windows shows it to MIDI 1.0 applications.

kind.description: engineClock: midi:clock:engine, the clock the engine generates from the sound card; its clock object reports that clock.

group.description: UMP group carrying this MIDI 1.0 port; 1 for virtual ports.

source.description: MIDI In: usable as a route source (virtual ports: input enabled).

destination.description: MIDI Out: usable as a route destination (virtual ports: output enabled).

online.description: Port present, or virtual port created.

open.description: The engine holds a connection to the port's endpoint; it opens an endpoint only when an enabled route uses one of its ports.

inputEndpointId.description: Virtual ports: endpoint of "<name> In", or null when input is off.

outputEndpointId.description: Virtual ports: endpoint of "<name> Out", or null when output is off.

received.description: MIDI 1.0 messages that arrived from the port since engine start, routed or not.

sent.description: MIDI 1.0 messages the engine delivered to the port since engine start.

activity.description: Every MIDI 1.0 message from the port except timing clock (F8) and active sensing (FE).

clock.description: Timing clock (F8) arriving from the port. running: a tick arrived less than 1 s ago. bpm: smoothed tempo at 24 ticks per quarter note, null until 2 ticks or when stopped. echoSuspected: the engine also sends clock to this port, so these ticks may be its own clock coming back (MIDI thru) rather than a real source. transport: last start (FA), continue (FB) or stop (FC).

active.description: Enabled, both ports present and open, source can send and destination can receive.

reclocked.description: Clock ticks re-emitted on the sound card grid (reclock routes).

anyOf.description: Read-only ASIO client status. Callback and exchange counters are since the most recent client start. An exchanged block may contain silence; these counters do not detect audible signal.

available.description: Whether the driver's shared client-status record could be read.

stable.description: Whether the callback counters came from one coherent snapshot.

callbackCount.description: ASIO callbacks observed by this client since start.

successfulExchangeCount.description: Callbacks that exchanged a complete block with the Timox engine.

lastCallbackAgeMs.description: Age of the most recent callback at this API read; null if none was observed or timing is unavailable.

processCpuPercent.description: Windows process CPU averaged across all active logical processors. Null until two process-time samples are available.

processCpuWindowMs.description: Elapsed wall time between process CPU samples. Null until the first measurement.

midi.description: null for audio adherents. MIDI adherents are MIDI 1.0 only; application ports report which of In/Out are enabled.

kind.description: application: an engine-owned MIDI application port (no process identity is claimed). engine: the engine itself, owner of the generated MIDI clock.

medium.description: Present on MIDI links; absent on audio links.

pwarClient.description: Existing supervised PWAR status payload; PID identifies only the current supervisor claim, not a proven process-instance merge.

kind.description: A processLoopback bridge creates an app audio copy owned by Timox and adds it as a separate graph source; it does not create a Timox ASIO client connection or redirect playback. The same process may also appear separately as an ASIO client if it opens the Timox virtual driver.

processId.description: Process whose shared Windows audio Timox copies into a separate graph source. This does not establish that the process opened the Timox ASIO driver.

processCreationTime.description: Decimal process creation timestamp paired with processId to distinguish this process instance from another process reusing the PID.

processImagePath.description: Executable image path paired with processId and processCreationTime to validate the process selected for copying; it does not identify the process's audio API.

wasapiBridgeConfigurations.description: IDs must be unique (validated transactionally by the server). Omission in apply preserves saved bridges; [] removes all.

containerId.description: Windows hardware container ID used to group related capture and render endpoints; null if unavailable.

windowsAudioApplication.description: A process with an active render session in the Windows shared audio mixer. This does not indicate whether the process opened TimoxVasio ASIO or which Windows audio API it selected.

processId.description: PID of the process that owns the shared render session; use with creationTime to distinguish process instances.

creationTime.description: Process creation time as a decimal string; paired with processId to identify this process instance.

imagePath.description: Executable image path for the process owning the shared render session.

displayName.description: Windows audio-session display name; it may differ from the executable name.

renderEndpoints.description: Windows output endpoints associated with the shared render session; this does not identify the audio API used by the process.

windowsAudioApplicationInventoryError.description: Null when enumeration succeeded; otherwise contains the inventory error. An empty applications array with an error does not mean that no sessions exist.

error.description: Signed 32-bit HRESULT; negative values indicate failure.

controlBacklogUpdates.description: Cumulative PI observations forced after 100 ms of unfinished draining in this generation; not an audio-loss count. Optional on earlier API 1.1 engines.

correctionPpm.description: (ratio / nominalRatio - 1) * 1e6; null without an effective generation.

rejectedFrames.description: Graph-rate rejected writes, including retried frames.

silencedFrames.description: Graph-rate missing read frames zero-padded by IO.

generationId.description: Decimal uint64 string preserves exact identity in JavaScript. 0 means no generation.

clients.description: Processes directly attached through TimoxVasio ASIO. A client is listed even when it has not allocated any channels yet; empty inputChannels and outputChannels arrays mean no routable ASIO ports are allocated, not that no client is attached.

pid.description: Process ID of the application that opened the TimoxVasio ASIO driver.

processName.description: Executable name of the direct ASIO client process.

processCpuPercent.description: Windows process CPU averaged across all active logical processors. Null until two process-time samples are available.

processCpuWindowMs.description: Elapsed wall time between process CPU samples. Null until the first measurement.

inputChannels.description: ASIO input channels allocated by createBuffers; these are destinations for graph routes. May be empty while the ASIO client remains attached.

outputChannels.description: ASIO output channels allocated by createBuffers; these are sources for graph routes. May be empty while the ASIO client remains attached.

activity.description: Read-only ASIO client status. Callback and exchange counters are since the most recent client start. An exchanged block may contain silence; these counters do not detect audible signal.

available.description: Whether the driver's shared client-status record could be read.

stable.description: Whether the callback counters came from one coherent snapshot.

callbackCount.description: ASIO callbacks observed by this client since start.

successfulExchangeCount.description: Callbacks that exchanged a complete block with the Timox engine.

lastCallbackAgeMs.description: Age of the most recent callback at this API read; null if none was observed or timing is unavailable.

processCreationTime.description: Windows FILETIME decimal string. Null when process identity cannot be read; PID alone is only runtime-scoped.

wasapiProcessLoopback.description: Whether the engine can create a separate graph source from one Windows process tree's shared audio.

configuredRoutes.description: All saved routes, including application routes waiting for a client with an active channel.

bufferHealth.description: A completed observation window of the physical ASIO callback. Null when no window has been observed in the current running session. Delayed starts are scheduling observations, not proof of audible dropouts.
